solutionSql:
SELECT s.customer_id, SUM(i.amount) AS billed_amount
FROM invoices AS i
JOIN shipments AS s ON s.id = i.shipment_id
GROUP BY s.customer_id
ORDER BY s.customer_id;

ambiguities.readingChosen: One row per customer that has at least one invoice (inner join from invoices).
ambiguities.alternativeReading: One row for every customer in the customers table, with NULL or 0 for customers without invoices (customers 7 and 8 here).

ambiguities.phrase: the total of the amount column over every invoice whose shipment belongs to that customer
ambiguities.readingChosen: Every invoice counts, including invoices on cancelled shipments.
ambiguities.alternativeReading: Exclude invoices whose shipment is cancelled; the totals change.

notes: Under the literal every-invoice wording, cancelled-shipment invoices count. Customers 7 and 8 have no shipments or invoices, so they are absent.
